construct: A unilateral medial medullary lesion affects corticospinal fibers in the pyramid before their caudal decussation, the already-crossed dorsal-column fibers ascending in the medial lemniscus, and ipsilateral hypoglossal fascicles. This produces contralateral weakness, contralateral loss of vibration/proprioception, and ipsilateral tongue weakness.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Left hemiparesis and left loss of vibration/proprioception with right tongue deviation localize to a right medial medullary lesion involving corticospinal fibers, medial lemniscus, and hypoglossal fascicles.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A lateral medullary lesion would preferentially cause nucleus ambiguus dysfunction, ipsilateral facial pain-temperature loss, Horner syndrome, and ataxia rather than the medial motor-dorsal-column-hypoglossal triad.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Ipsilateral hypoglossal LMN weakness fixes the lesion on the right, while the body deficits are contralateral because of the relevant crossing anatomy; the right medial triad is uniquely correct.
